Enhanced due diligence is required at onboarding, on any change of beneficial ownership, and on every new director or UBO appointment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial Registration Portal - https://gcis.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must be in traditional Chinese characters. An English name is auxiliary and not a substitute for the Chinese legal name. The name must identify the company type (usually 有限公司 or 股份有限公司) and must not create confusion with an existing or officially protected name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name pre-approval is valid for 180 days from issuance and is not extendable; if incorporation is not completed within that window, a new name pre-approval application is required. Upon an adverse name decision, the applicant or its Taiwan counsel may file an administrative appeal (訴願) with the MOEA within 30 days of service of the written rejection, explaining the reasons and proposing an alternative acceptable name. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file an administrative action with the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months of service of the appeal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not accepted as the sole registered office for a licensed Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in government-relations advisory and lobbying activities. The MOEA registration and the Lobbying Act registration require a genuine physical place of business in Taiwan; mail-forwarding or virtual-office services may only supplement, not replace, the registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% to 55% within the first two years due to the Lobbying Act registration regime and enhanced AML/CFT supervision of lobbying and government-relations businesses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Taiwan jurisdiction (公司法, as amended) — Articles 6, 12, 98-113, 150-154, 387 and 410; Foreign Investment Statute (外國人投資條例) Articles 7, 8 and 11; Regulations Governing Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法), where a mainland Chinese shareholder participates; Business Tax Act (加值型及非加值型營業稅法) Article 28 for tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署), Taiwan jurisdiction — sole registry for limited company incorporation; filings accepted via the MOEA one-stop online portal (公司與商業一站式申請作業) or the Taipei municipal commerce office counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) filed under Company Act Article 387, culminating in the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company (Company Act Articles 100 and 156, post-2018 reform); the shareholders' agreement may fix capital at any commercially justified amount. Full subscribed capital must be deposited in a provisional bank account opened in the company's name in Taiwan and evidenced by a bank-issued capital certificate; no escrow account is required for services-sector joint ventures, but inward foreign-currency remittance must conform to the investment approval schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: THAT the subscribers ratify the Articles of Incorporation and confirm subscription of the registered capital set forth therein; THAT the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Address], Taiwan, with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs as the filing registry; THAT the shareholders confirm payment of share capital and approve the issuance of shares as set out in the subscription schedule; THAT [Name] be appointed Director and Chairman, [Name] General Manager, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting; AND THAT the Chairman and Secretary are jointly authorized to execute and file all incorporation documents and licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署), Taiwan — online Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Application (公司名稱及所營事業預查申請) via the MOEA one-stop online portal; propose at least three candidate names in the format 'Taiwan + trade name + Limited Company'; enumerate the business scope to include government affairs consulting and permitted lobbying services; pay the NT$300 fee and retain the approval letter valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Application Form
Identification documents (passports/residence permits) of all shareholders
Corporate authorization letter and certificate of incorporation of any corporate shareholder
Skeletal Articles of Incorporation stating proposed business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identity or confusing similarity under the Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Rules, file an amended application with alternative names within 10 working days; a contested rejection may be appealed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investor Investment and JV Contract Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Division, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign and/or mainland Chinese shareholders' investment application with the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture contract and shareholders' agreement before any capital remittance or incorporation filing. Mainland China origin investors are screened under the Regulations Governing Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors; verify the government-affairs consulting scope (ISIC 7020) is absent from the Negative List, or restructure the investment if restricted. Obtain the written investment approval letter.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of incorporation of each investor
Audited financial statements of the investing entities (latest fiscal year)
Joint venture contract and shareholders' agreement (dual-language)
Business plan, investment schedule and source-of-funds declaration
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, supply supplementary explanations or revised JV documents within the statutory 60-day cure period; a final denial may be administratively appealed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Bank Capital Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed commercial bank in Taiwan; the account is opened in the proposed company's pre-approved name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account using the pre-approved name and deposit the full subscribed capital by each shareholder. The bank issues a Capital Certificate (存款餘額證明) evidencing the closing balance. Foreign-currency remittances are tagged against the investment approval letter; confirm the remittance channel with the bank for mainland China sourced funds.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application and company specimen seal
Shareholder identification and power of attorney
Inward remittance records and foreign exchange purchase memo
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, provide the source-of-funds ledger and a certified share-credit schedule; any material variance between approved and deposited capital requires an amended investment application.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration, Taiwan (財政部賦稅署); operational administration by the National Taxation Administration regional offices (各地區國稅局). Unified e-tax portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign enterprise (including a People's Republic of China Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture) establishing a Taiwan operation, the statutory TIN/VAT ID is the Taiwan Uniform Serial Number (統一編號). Procedure: (1) Apply to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs for approval of a branch office or a Taiwan-incorporated subsidiary; submit the foreign parent's incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, board resolution authorising the Taiwan establishment, and a notarised power of attorney, with authentication as required. (2) Upon MOEA approval, the Taiwan branch or subsidiary receives its Uniform Serial Number, which simultaneously serves as the tax identification number for both income tax and business tax purposes. (3) Within 15 days after the MOEA registration or before commencing business, file business tax registration (營業登記) with the local National Taxation Administration, using the issued Uniform Serial Number, and obtain the sales tax registration certificate. (4) Register for the electronic uniform invoice (電子發票) system, and, because the activity is government-affairs lobbying, obtain the applicable industry or lobbying registration licence prior to rendering regulated services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not recognise US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch flow-through elections. A foreign investor may choose the corporate form of a Taiwan-incorporated subsidiary, which is a Taiwan-resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed on its worldwide income, or a Taiwan branch, which is a non-resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed on Taiwan-source income only; this choice is made through corporate-law registration, not a tax classification election. Other available elections are limited to procedural VAT/invoice matters, such as the use of electronic invoices and the filing of business tax returns under the credit method.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold. Every business selling goods or services within the Taiwan territory is required to register for business tax before commencing business. A small-scale business (monthly taxable sales below NT$80,000 for goods or NT$40,000 for services) may enjoy a preferential 1% business tax rate, but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates a Unified Invoice (統一發票) system. E-invoice (電子發票) issuance is mandatory for taxpayers designated by the Ministry of Finance and for all B2B transactions in qualifying sectors. E-invoice data must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Turnkey Platform within 48 hours for B2B invoices and within 7 days for B2C invoices. The platform provides central invoice-number assignment, API-based transmission for large taxpayers, real-time data matching against VAT returns, and automated audit trails. Physical fiscal stamping is not used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act applies to: (a) goods exported from Taiwan; (b) services provided in Taiwan that are used outside Taiwan, including cross-border advisory, trade policy analysis, and lobbying-related consulting services where the foreign stakeholder recipient is outside Taiwan and no substantive benefit is consumed within Taiwan; (c) services related to exported goods; and (d) international transport. For the government-affairs lobbying activity, zero-rating is available only if the services are performed for a foreign stakeholder, all lobbying activity is directed to foreign governmental bodies, and the consideration is received in foreign currency with robust documentation that the place of use is offshore. Domestic lobbying or consultancy benefiting persons in Taiwan remains taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) for physical goods and, where applicable, an electronic export services declaration
Uniform Invoice or export services invoice issued at zero rate
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Waybill evidencing export movement for goods
Foreign exchange settlement certificate (結匯證實書) or bank inward remittance advice for services
Signed service agreement or contract demonstrating the foreign recipient and the offshore-use condition
Power of attorney and lobbying registration evidence for the claimant entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Administration may audit zero-rated export claims. If non-qualification or false documentation is found, the tax authority reassesses the gross consideration at the standard 5% business tax, imposes daily interest from the original filing date, and applies a penalty of up to five times the underpaid tax under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act. Intentional fraudulent declaration, forged export documentation, or use of fictitious foreign-currency remittances may trigger criminal liability under the Tax Evasion Penalty Regulations and the Criminal Code, including imprisonment and loss of entitlement to future government procurement. The ordinary assessment and clawback window is five years from the date of filing; in fraud cases, criminal liability and recovery are not subject to the five-year cap.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), operating with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) for banking supervision and the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission (MOEAIC) for foreign investment approvals. Because the proposed investor is identified as China-linked, the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area and its implementing regulations must also be assessed before account opening, capital injection, or remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including trade in services, operating expenses, and approved profit distributions. Taiwan does not operate a general capital-account convertibility regime equivalent to unrestricted offshore movement of capital. Capital inflows, equity funding, shareholder loans, acquisitions, and repatriation of capital may require investment approval, documentary evidence, bank reporting, and transaction-purpose verification. A Taiwan company may distribute dividends only from legally distributable earnings after statutory accounts, tax clearance or withholding compliance, and corporate approvals. Dividends, service fees, interest, royalties, liquidation proceeds, and capital reductions paid to non-residents are subject to applicable Taiwan withholding tax, treaty relief conditions, transfer-pricing support, and authorized-bank processing. A China-linked investor presents an additional eligibility and national-security risk: Mainland Chinese investment, ownership, management participation, beneficial ownership, and service arrangements may be restricted or require prior approval, and a Taiwan bank may decline onboarding even where general foreign-investment rules would otherwise permit the structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be surrendered to the banking system or converted into New Taiwan dollars at a fixed ratio. Export and service-export receipts may generally be retained in foreign currency or converted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank, subject to accurate customs, invoice, contract, and transaction-purpose records. Foreign-exchange declarations or reporting may apply where the transaction is not a routine trade receipt, where the amount exceeds applicable thresholds, or where the transaction falls within CBC reporting rules. Banks may require evidence of the underlying export or service transaction, and suspicious, irregular, related-party, or China-linked receipts may be escalated under AML and cross-strait controls. No mandatory conversion percentage should be assumed; the bank's internal documentary and reporting requirements must be confirmed before implementation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Mega International Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.
Taipei Fubon Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for routine foreign-currency payments and treasury technology; low for core operating accounts, capital escrow, shareholder funding, or regulated collection of third-party funds. Taiwan does not provide a simple EU-style passportable electronic-money institution regime. Electronic payment institutions and payment processors are regulated under Taiwan financial laws and may be limited in stored-value issuance, payment collection, foreign-exchange activity, remittance, settlement, and third-party funds handling. An offshore digital EMI cannot be assumed to provide a lawful substitute for a Taiwan-authorized bank or permitted payment institution. The JV should use a Taiwan authorized bank for capital injection, payroll, taxes, dividends, trade receipts, and material supplier payments, with any fintech limited to bank-integrated technology services after legal and bank approval. Government-relations and lobbying receipts require enhanced source-of-funds and underlying-service documentation and must not be routed through accounts designed to conceal the payer, beneficial owner, or purpose.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote preliminary onboarding may be available, but it is not a reliable substitute for final bank approval. Taiwan banks commonly require original or certified corporate documents, verification of directors and authorized signatories, beneficial-owner identification, specimen signatures, board resolutions, and an in-person interview or notarized equivalent. The bank may require physical attendance by the Taiwan-resident responsible person, authorized representative, or controlling persons. Remote execution is more likely for an existing customer with a strong Taiwan banking relationship than for a newly incorporated China-linked JV. Mainland Chinese directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, or controllers may trigger enhanced review, additional approvals, restrictions, or refusal. Do not appoint a nominee or use an undisclosed control arrangement to avoid physical KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mainland China parent, shareholder, director, controller, or ultimate beneficial owner associated with a Taiwan entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete ownership chart from the Taiwan JV through every intermediate entity to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; certified constitutional documents; shareholder register; passports and residential evidence; board and shareholder resolutions; evidence of nationality and place of incorporation; MOEAIC or other competent-authority investment approval; cross-strait approval analysis; sanctions and politically exposed person screening; proof that no prohibited Mainland investment, nominee ownership, or undisclosed control exists; and a written legal memorandum addressing the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Government-affairs, lobbying, policy-advisory, or foreign-stakeholder engagement activity classified as medium-risk enhanced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business plan; statutory license, registration, or filing evidence under the Taiwan Lobbying Act and other applicable professional or sector rules; client and payer list; signed engagement letters; scope-of-work descriptions; fee schedules; invoices; deliverable examples; conflict-of-interest policy; anti-bribery and anti-corruption policy; political-exposure screening; beneficial-owner information for each client; evidence that payments are commercial advisory fees rather than political contributions, facilitation payments, or undisclosed intermediary compensation; and transaction monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital described ambiguously as equity, shareholder loan, service fee, or intercompany settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed joint-venture agreement, articles, capitalization table, investment approval, board resolution, subscription agreement or loan agreement, funds-flow memorandum, remitter account statement, proof of source of funds, tax analysis, transfer-pricing support, bank payment-purpose declaration, and confirmation that the remittance amount matches the approved capital or contractual obligation. Maintain separate accounting and bank references for equity, debt, revenue, reimbursements, and expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual third-party remitter, payment from an offshore account, layered intermediary, or payment inconsistent with the invoiced customer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a three-party or agency agreement explaining the payment path; full identity and beneficial ownership documents for the remitter, customer, and intermediary; commercial rationale for third-party settlement; invoices and acceptance evidence; bank statements showing the source of funds; sanctions, AML, and adverse-media screening; tax treatment; and a written bank pre-clearance where practicable. Reject unexplained third-party payments and cash settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border service receipts without tangible deliverables or with vague descriptions such as consulting or facilitation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain the master services agreement, work orders, timesheets, meeting records, reports, correspondence, travel records, deliverables, customer acceptance, invoice, tax invoice, pricing benchmark, transfer-pricing file, and evidence of the personnel and resources performing the work. Use precise payment descriptions and ensure the activity is legally permitted under Taiwan licensing, lobbying, public-affairs, anti-corruption, and foreign-agent restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions, export-control, dual-use, military, state-owned-enterprise, or politically exposed counterparty exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Conduct documented screening against Taiwan, United Nations, United States, European Union, United Kingdom, and bank-specific sanctions lists as contractually or operationally relevant; identify government ownership and politically exposed persons; obtain end-use and end-user certifications; retain compliance approvals; apply escalation thresholds; and prohibit transactions lacking sufficient counterparty and purpose information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested use of personal accounts, nominee accounts, virtual IBANs, cash, cryptocurrency, or offshore wallets for corporate funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopt a treasury policy requiring accounts in the JV's legal name, dual authorization, beneficiary verification, approved bank rails, monthly reconciliations, and prohibition of personal or anonymous settlement. Provide the bank with the policy, signatory matrix, internal controls, and evidence that all prior receipts were regularized and correctly booked.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit remittance, management fee, royalty, interest, or capital reduction to a non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited or approved financial statements, distributable-profit calculation, shareholder and board resolutions, withholding-tax computation, treaty-residence certificate where relief is claimed, transfer-pricing report, intercompany agreement, evidence of actual services or financing, regulatory approvals, proof of tax filing or payment, and the bank's remittance application. Confirm that the payment is not a disguised distribution or prohibited cross-strait transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity capital through a Taiwan authorized foreign-exchange bank into a dedicated capital account or approved corporate account in the exact legal name of the JV. Obtain any required MOEAIC, cross-strait, sector, and corporate approvals before remittance. The remitter should be the approved shareholder or an expressly approved funding vehicle, not an unrelated third party. Use an accurate payment-purpose code and narrative identifying equity subscription, capital contribution, or approved shareholder loan; do not describe capital as consulting revenue or reimbursement. Provide the bank with the investment approval, subscription or loan agreement, capitalization table, board resolutions, remitter proof of funds, beneficial-owner information, and expected funds-flow schedule. The bank must validate the remittance, report or declare it where required, and complete capital verification or registration procedures. Reconcile the incoming wire to the accounting ledger and maintain evidence for future dividend, loan-repayment, or capital-repatriation transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Taiwan authorized-bank accounts for supplier, contractor, payroll, tax, and approved cross-border service payments. For ordinary commercial payments, use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's current ISO 20022 equivalent with complete originator, beneficiary, invoice, contract, currency, amount, and purpose information. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or open-account payment only after the bank confirms the transaction is within its permitted trade-finance scope. Match every payment to a purchase order, invoice, customs or service evidence, contract, and approved beneficiary account. For lobbying and policy-advisory payments, identify the actual service, client, beneficiary, and authorized intermediary; avoid success fees or payment instructions that could constitute bribery, concealed political funding, or unauthorized third-party settlement. The bank may require enhanced review for China-linked beneficiaries, sensitive sectors, government counterparties, or payments involving offshore intermediaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts with an authorized Taiwan bank, limited to documented or reasonably forecast commercial exposures and subject to bank suitability, credit, collateral, and transaction-documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through an authorized bank for eligible currencies and counterparties, subject to Taiwan regulatory permissions, bank product approval, master documentation, and genuine underlying exposure. They should not be used for speculative trading or disguised capital transfers.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps may be available through an authorized Taiwan bank for documented financing or operating exposures, subject to derivative appropriateness assessment, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral and credit terms, accounting controls, and regulatory reporting.

Foreign-exchange options or structured hedges may be available only where the bank approves the product as suitable and the company can demonstrate a genuine exposure, risk capacity, valuation controls, and full understanding of contingent obligations. The JV should prohibit leveraged or speculative structures without board approval and independent treasury review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting adoption of business report, audited financial statements, and profit appropriation/loss-offset proposal; certified minutes filed to MOEA Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); MOEA filing within 15 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA may order the directors to convene a meeting within a specified period; each responsible director is subject to a fine of NT$10,000–50,000; persistent failure can lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of audited financial statements and business report with MOEA after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office; tax copy lodged with the National Taxation Bureau with the annual income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after AGM approval and in all cases before the end of the 6-month statutory window (30 June for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors are liable to fines and rectification orders; continued failure to file true financial statements may be treated as cause for compulsory dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax annual return and accompanying financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local tax bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 May through 31 May following the tax year; special accounting year-end filings due within 5 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers estimated assessment and statutory penalties; underreported tax may be additionally assessed; overdue tax is referred for compulsory execution and, if unresolved, can lead to suspension of business and deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operation Report for approved Sino-Foreign JV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 5 months after fiscal year-end (by 31 May for calendar-year filers), with audited financial statements where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a rectification notice, suspension of investment incentives, revocation of foreign investment approval, and ultimately company deregistration or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and sign-off covering Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book, and beneficial-owner records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary/governance officer; registers kept on site and produced to MOEA, tax authorities and inspectors on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registers updated within 15 days of any share transfer or directorship change; full audit completed before the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers may be fined and ordered to correct the registers; false or incomplete records can invalidate reliance on limited-liability defenses and contribute to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 1 million), when the company is a public company or financial institution, or when MOEA or the foreign investment approval requires an audit opinion; foreign-invested JVs must attach a CPA-certified financial statement to the annual foreign investment report when the prescribed turnover or investment threshold is met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply Taiwan-IFRS (T-IFRS); non-public companies apply Republic of China GAAP under the Business Entity Accounting Act and related rules; eligible small and medium enterprises may adopt Taiwan SME GAAP. Tax records must also follow the retention and verification requirements of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a non-public foreign-invested JV in Taiwan, there is no separate public annual UBO return. The company must maintain a current Register of Members and update it within 15 days of any share transfer. At each annual general meeting, the board confirms the register and any share transfers; the annual foreign investment report repeats this ownership confirmation to the Investment Commission. For AML compliance, beneficial-owner information must be collected, verified and made available to competent authorities and financial institutions upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,800 per annum for registered address and local corporate secretary/agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–9,000 per annum for a typical non-public JV, increasing with cross-border transaction complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on Taiwan-sourced taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax incentives may include approved investment tax credits, accelerated depreciation, research and development credits, industrial innovation incentives, and qualifying free-trade-zone or science-park incentives. Incentives are activity-specific, approval-dependent, and subject to statutory ceilings. A Taiwan company generally may carry qualifying business losses forward for up to 10 years if statutory accounting, filing, and certification conditions are satisfied; the requested schema value is 5 years and must be reconciled against the applicable Taiwan rule before filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Annual Income Tax Return, filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing system for profit-seeking enterprises (e-filing software and online submission portal administered by the National Taxation Bureau)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed from 1 May through 31 May of the following year for a calendar-year taxpayer. A taxpayer with a non-calendar fiscal year files within the fifth month after fiscal year-end. An extension may be available where statutory conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified Business Number, legal name, registered address, fiscal year, responsible person, accounting period, tax agent, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Taiwan entity's own registration number. A foreign shareholder's tax identification number does not replace the Taiwan entity's Unified Business Number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Income statement and taxable income reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book revenue, operating costs, operating expenses, non-operating income, non-deductible expenses, tax adjustments, and taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Taiwan entity's worldwide income under Taiwan corporate tax rules, subject to foreign tax credit limitations and applicable source rules. Separate shareholder-level income from company income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party identities, transaction categories, amounts, pricing methods, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border transactions with the Mainland China parent, affiliates, directors, and controlled service providers. Maintain contemporaneous support for arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign-source income and foreign tax credit schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income, foreign taxes paid, supporting tax certificates, and credit limitation computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only taxes legally imposed and actually paid, supported by official foreign tax documents and translated where required. Taiwan has no operative comprehensive income tax treaty with Mainland China for ordinary treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Depreciation, amortization, provisions, and tax incentive schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation, amortization, reserves, provisions, investment credits, research credits, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Taiwan tax useful lives and documentary requirements. Book treatment alone does not establish tax deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed losses, utilization, remaining balance, and expiration period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses formally reported and eligible under Taiwan requirements, including timely filing, complete books, and required audit or certification conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, installments, withholding credits, and payment information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax, credits, provisional payments, withholding credits, balance payable, refund claim, and payment account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile shareholder withholding, service-fee withholding, interest, royalties, provisional payments, and any tax withheld by Taiwan payers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Responsible-person declaration, certified financial statements where required, audit report, related-party schedules, and supporting documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent documents should be retained with certified translations where requested. Certification by a Taiwan-certified public accountant may be mandatory based on size, industry, public-company status, or other statutory criteria.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a surcharge of 10% of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Failure to file after notice may attract a 20% surcharge with higher statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Late payment may incur a surcharge calculated by statutory two-day periods, capped under the Tax Collection Act, followed by interest and compulsory collection. Understatement can trigger additional tax, interest, and penalties; intentional evasion may create criminal exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Provisional Income Tax Return, Taiwan Ministry of Finance electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during September for the first six months of a calendar year, subject to the statutory filing window and available exemptions. The provisional payment is credited against annual corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income and deductible expenses for the first six months, with statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Taiwan company's actual Taiwan-period results and identify related-party transactions occurring during the provisional period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable corporate tax rate, less permitted credits and payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use the shareholder's foreign tax position to reduce the Taiwan entity's provisional tax unless a statutory Taiwan credit is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment reference, tax paid, prior credits, and balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank evidence and reconcile the provisional payment to the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incorrect provisional filing may result in additional tax, interest, administrative penalties, and loss of filing or loss-utilization benefits where statutory conditions are not met. Applicability and exemptions must be checked against the taxpayer's status and accounting certification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding Tax Statement and Withholding Tax Return, Taiwan electronic withholding filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or event-based, depending on payment type
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax withheld is generally remitted within the statutory period following payment, allocation, or constructive payment, commonly by the tenth day of the following month. Annual withholding statements are generally issued and filed by the statutory January deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payee name, address, tax identification number, residency status, and beneficial-owner information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain the Mainland parent or other foreign payee's legal identity, tax residence certificate, beneficial-owner declaration, and payment-basis documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend, interest, royalty, professional service fee, commission, rent, or other payment category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify according to Taiwan source rules and substance, not merely contractual labels. Services performed in Taiwan may create Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Gross payment, applicable rate, and tax withheld
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount, statutory or approved treaty rate, tax withheld, remittance date, and currency conversion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the domestic rate unless reduced treatment has been validly obtained. Retain exchange-rate methodology and payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Approval number, tax residence certificate reference, relief basis, and supporting documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taiwan relief generally requires documentary substantiation and, where applicable, advance approval by the competent tax authority. Mainland China cannot be treated as a treaty jurisdiction without a legally effective applicable arrangement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold, under-withholding, late remittance, incorrect statements, or failure to issue certificates can make the Taiwan payer liable for the unwithheld tax, interest, and administrative penalties. Intentional concealment or false documentation may create criminal tax exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident individual, foreign company, or other nonresident recipient, subject to applicable exemptions or legally effective treaty relief. Dividends to Taiwan-resident companies are generally governed by separate domestic rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, confirm whether an effective Taiwan tax treaty or tax agreement applies, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence, establish beneficial ownership and substantive entitlement, document the payment and anti-avoidance position, and submit any required application to the competent National Taxation Bureau. The Taiwan payer should not apply a reduced rate solely on receipt of a foreign certificate unless the applicable rules permit self-assessment. Mainland China should be treated as non-treaty for ordinary Taiwan withholding purposes unless a specific effective arrangement applies to the payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Taiwan withholding is generally 20% on royalties paid to nonresidents and generally 20% on interest paid to nonresidents, subject to category-specific statutory rates, exemptions, approved reductions, and effective treaty rates. Certain interest categories, including qualifying bonds, bank deposits, or approved financial instruments, may have different domestic rates. Treaty rates vary by instrument and treaty and must be confirmed for the payee's residence jurisdiction. Payments to Mainland China generally require domestic Taiwan analysis rather than assumed treaty reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan generally requires a Local File for reportable controlled transactions unless an exemption or simplified documentation rule applies. A principal threshold for comprehensive transfer-pricing documentation is annual net revenue and non-operating income of at least NT$3 billion or aggregate cross-border controlled transactions of at least NT$1.5 billion, with transaction-type and other statutory tests also relevant. A Master File is generally relevant where the enterprise meets the NT$3 billion revenue threshold and the applicable aggregate cross-border controlled-transaction threshold. Country-by-Country Reporting may apply to Taiwan constituent entities of multinational enterprise groups meeting the NT$27 billion consolidated revenue threshold. Thresholds and exemptions must be checked for the relevant fiscal year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods permitted by Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations where the prescribed methods cannot reliably be applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless relevant under transfer-pricing rules, anti-avoidance principles, beneficial-ownership analysis, source-of-income rules, tax treaty access, deductibility, and controlled foreign company rules. The entity should demonstrate Taiwan decision-making, personnel, premises, functions, assets, risks, books, bank activity, and commercial purpose appropriate to its government-relations advisory and lobbying activities. Artificial conduit arrangements, circular payments, nominee directors, and undocumented shareholder services are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Mainland China investment or prohibited foreign investment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating or funding a Taiwan joint venture through Mainland Chinese capital, personnel, control rights, or contractual arrangements without the approvals required under Taiwan laws governing Mainland Area investment and foreign investment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, orders to withdraw or correct the investment, suspension or revocation of investment approval, forced disposal of shares, and possible restrictions on future investment. The amount depends on the violated statute and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face administrative liability, civil damages, disqualification consequences, and criminal liability where false filings, evasion of approval, or prohibited conduct is involved. Travel restrictions or imprisonment are not automatic and require statutory grounds and judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery and improper influence involving public officials
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering, promising, authorizing, reimbursing, or concealing money, gifts, hospitality, employment, political contributions, or other benefits to influence a public official, public procurement, regulatory decision, permit, or government contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Taiwan anti-corruption and Criminal Code provisions; penalties may include imprisonment and fines, forfeiture of illicit benefits, debarment, and corporate administrative consequences. Penalty level depends on the official's status, benefit amount, intent, and transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, employees, agents, and beneficial owners may be prosecuted personally. Corporate authorization, knowledge, acquiescence, or failure to maintain controls may support corporate and individual liability. Civil restitution and forfeiture may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unregistered or noncompliant lobbying and government-affairs activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting regulated lobbying without required registration, filing inaccurate lobbying reports, failing to disclose the principal, using prohibited intermediaries, or disguising lobbying expenditure as consulting, donations, entertainment, or political payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, orders to correct, public disclosure, suspension or cancellation of registration, and possible referral for criminal investigation where bribery, fraud, or false documents are involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and lobbyists may incur personal administrative or criminal liability for false reports, concealed principals, or prohibited conduct. Corporate veil piercing is fact-specific and is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing revenue, fabricating expenses, issuing or accepting false invoices, misclassifying lobbying payments, concealing beneficial owners, manipulating transfer prices, or claiming unsupported foreign tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, late-payment interest, administrative fines, denial of deductions or credits, compulsory collection, and criminal prosecution for intentional evasion or fraudulent methods under Taiwan tax laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons, accountants, signatories, and participants may face criminal imprisonment and fines, civil restitution, forfeiture, and tax collection against responsible persons where statutory conditions are satisfied. Travel bans may be imposed in appropriate collection or criminal proceedings; they are not an automatic tax consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging artificial management or government-relations fees, shifting profits to Mainland China, failing to perform services, using non-arm's-length royalties or interest, or omitting related-party disclosures and documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan tax authority adjustment to taxable income, denial of deductions, deemed income or withholding adjustments, penalties for inaccurate returns, interest, and possible anti-avoidance review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may incur liability for intentional false records, fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, or participation in evasion. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments alone do not automatically create imprisonment or veil piercing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained retainers, routing funds through personal or nominee accounts, structuring payments, dealing with sanctioned or high-risk counterparties, failing to identify beneficial owners, or ignoring suspicious transactions connected to political influence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transaction reporting, account freezing, confiscation, administrative fines, business restrictions, and criminal liability for money laundering or predicate offenses. Penalties depend on amount, knowledge, concealment, and participation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, employees, and agents may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly participate, facilitate, conceal, or fail to perform legally required controls. Assets may be confiscated and civil restitution may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing strategic government-affairs services, technology, information, or financial support to sanctioned persons, restricted entities, or prohibited Mainland-related activities without required authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties, license suspension, transaction prohibition, asset blocking, confiscation, and criminal prosecution under applicable Taiwan sanctions, national-security, trade, and export-control laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face criminal liability, fines, confiscation, management disqualification, and civil claims. Imprisonment and travel restrictions depend on the specific offense and judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using company funds for undisclosed political influence, related-party benefits, personal expenses, kickbacks, or transactions lacking board approval and commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil damages, disgorgement, shareholder claims, accounting sanctions, administrative penalties, and criminal breach-of-trust or misappropriation charges where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be jointly liable for damages, restitution, disgorgement, and criminal penalties. Veil piercing requires abuse of the company, commingling, fraud, or another legally recognized basis; it is not presumed from ownership or control alone.
